data.title: Trump admin urged Venezuela, Iraq to quit OPEC, blocked Venezuela’s membership dues: Reuters
data.description:
The Trump administration encouraged Venezuela and Iraq to consider leaving OPEC earlier this year and prevented Venezuela from paying its annual membership dues to the group, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

The moves targeted two of OPEC's five founding members, marking an unusually direct challenge to an organization President Donald Trump has long accused of keeping oil prices artificially high.

US officials were pushing for greater oil production and investment in both countries at the time, and some worried OPEC production limits could eventually constrain those ambitions, the report said.

The US pressure on Venezuela went far enough that Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman intervened this summer, persuading the Trump administration not to press the issue further, people familiar with the matter said.

In Iraq, Prime Minister ‌Ali Faleh al-Zaidi raised the possibility of leaving OPEC at a government meeting this summer after discussions with US officials who encouraged the idea, the report added.

The US State Department did not answer questions about whether it had prevented Venezuela from paying its OPEC membership fee. But it ​confirmed Washington has the power to decide on Venezuela’s use of state funds, now held in a US-controlled account set up after Maduro's removal, the report said.

"The Department receives disbursement requests from the interim Venezuelan government and reviews the requests, including against a list of approved and prohibited uses of ​the foreign Government Deposit Funds," a State Department official told Reuters.

The official said that it was possible that lower-level US officials had raised the question of leaving OPEC with Venezuela's government earlier this year, but that "it has ⁠not been among the issues raised by high-level officials."

The State Department's conversations with Iraq, meanwhile, "have focused on improving energy infrastructure to increase production and transportation of energy, not OPEC," the official told the new agency.

data.title: Meituan Q3 revenue meets estimates as delivery demand offsets competition
data.description:
Food delivery company Meituan on Friday ​reported revenue and profit that were in line with or slightly outpaced market estimates as strong demand for its core food delivery services in summer and cost-control measures helped offset intensifying competition in China's on-demand retail market.

Since Alibaba's Taobao and JD.com entered the instant-retail market with new platforms in early 2025, Meituan has spent more than a year contending with pressure on revenue growth and profitability.

Instant retail, or quick commerce, refers to online orders for food, bubble tea and other everyday essentials that are delivered within 60 minutes.

Meituan's revenue for the quarter that ended on September 30 reached 115.56 billion yuan ($17.37 billion), ​a 21.6% rise ​from a ⁠year earlier, outpacing analyst expectations.

Its adjusted net profit was 1.85 billion yuan, down from ​last quarter's 2.52 billion yuan.

China's market regulator was investigating Meituan unit Beijing Sankuai Information Technology for ‌suspected violations of unfair competition laws, according to a state media report in September.

data.title: Entain Agrees To AU$185 Mln Settlement With AUSTRAC Over AML Breaches
data.description:
LONDON (dpa-AFX) - Entain Plc (ENT.L), a sports betting and gaming group, on Friday announced that its Australian subsidiary, Entain Group Pty Ltd, has reached a preliminary agreement with the Australian Transaction Reports and Analysis Centre or AUSTRAC.

The agreement proposes a settlement of AU$185 million to resolve civil penalty proceedings.

The proceedings relate to alleged breaches of Australia's Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2006 between December 2018 and August 2024.

Under the proposed settlement, Entain Australia will pay a civil penalty of AU$185 million, plus AUSTRAC's legal costs.

The settlement remains subject to approval by the company's Board, AUSTRAC and the Federal Court of Australia.

The penalty is expected to be paid in full in late December.

The company said it has fully cooperated with AUSTRAC and completed significant improvements to its Australian subsidiary's anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing systems, processes and controls.

On Thursday, Entain closed trading 2.09% higher at GBp 454.40 on the London Stock Exchange.

data.title: Meituan Posts Earnings Beat as Price War Cools
data.description:
By Tracy Qu

Meituan's profit was largely stable sequentially amid higher revenue in the third quarter as China's top food-delivery company continued to recover from a brutal price war.

The Beijing-based company on Friday said net profit was 2.07 billion yuan, equivalent to $310.7 million, for the three months ended September. It recorded a 2.15 billion yuan net profit in the second quarter and net loss of 18.63 billion yuan a year ago.

Revenue climbed 22% from a year earlier to 115.55 billion yuan.

The results beat market expectations. Analysts had expected net profit of 354.7 million yuan on revenue of 113.56 billion yuan, according to a FactSet-compiled consensus.

Meituan has been locked in a food-delivery price war since last year as Alibaba Group and JD.com pushed to gain more market share. Competition has normalized in recent quarters.

Write to Tracy Qu at tracy.qu@wsj.com
